<!-- pr-reviewer: e7ae538a3d4b273cf00b75653c21eed9ab47402e -->
**Review of head e7ae538a3: the entry follows the maintainer decision. It is not ready: four items to fix and the gate to complete.** Two independent reads (one of them by the worker that made the held implementation on `issue/3567-ramp-entry-max`), not built by the reviewer. I set `needs-rework` and made the PR a draft: a PR opens as a draft, and this one had no review.

## What is correct
- At a pass start whose column is still solid, the tool comes down by the existing zig-zag ramp on the pass itself, at the ramp angle of the entry or 3 degrees, from the material top plus the plunge height. The last leg lands on the pass start at the floor, and the whole pass is then cut at depth. No material stays below the ramp.
- Each ramp point is on the proved pass. It cannot get to the part wall or to a "Do not touch" item.
- The flag is set only for Outside with Waterline or Offset rings. Auto, Inside, rest machining, Adaptive, Bore and Circular do not change. The completeness guard and `RINGS_FALLBACK` do not change. No golden and no catalog program is in the diff.
- No new `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`. The zig-zag code guards a zero length, an angle of zero and NaN.
- The pin of the held implementation (the late-entry pin at 0.00 mm2, the ramp angle, the floor below the ramp) passes on this head; `pass_start_levels` is 7 of 7.

## To fix on this branch
1. **A silent plunge stays possible** (`ladder_links.rs:191`). When the pass is too short for the ramp, `ramp_fallback` returns `None` and the old helix or plunge runs with no note. That is the fault of #3567 again, with no message. Wanted: a named note, and the fallback to the Auto order with the `StrategyFallback` warning (the note carries `RINGS_FALLBACK`), or a refusal. Pin it with a short pass.
2. **The pin cannot tell a ramp from a steep feed** (`pass_start_engagement.rs:131`). It counts only `MoveKind::Plunge` and a descending arc. A straight feed at 60 degrees, or a vertical feed, passes as a ramp. Wanted: a slope limit (the ramp angle plus a small tolerance), and an assert that a ramp did run, so that the pin cannot pass with no ramp.
3. **A replaced entry has no note.** A user who selected Plunge or Helix gets the ramp at a dead end with no message. The law of #2265 gives a named note for a stand-in entry (`ladder_links.rs:200-203`). Add the note one time for each operation.
4. **Say what the ramp is.** At a dead end about 83 percent of the tool disc is in uncut stock (41.6 mm2 of 50.3 mm2 for each of the 8 starts). The zig-zag thus cuts a slot at nearly the full tool width, at 3 degrees. That is a normal entry, and it is what the maintainer decision permits ("a ramp along the pass"). But the decision file says only "engages in a gradual way", and the pin reads 0.00 mm2 because ramp moves are not counted, not because no stock is cut. Write it plainly in the decision file, in the body and in the `Changelog:` line. Name 2D Pocket with Outside also: it gets the ramp through `pocket_over_with_relief`, and the changelog names only 2D Offset.
5. `levels.rs` goes from 431 to 441 lines (over the limit before this PR). Do not add to it: move the new lines to the module that holds the entry.
6. Draft PR #3566 adds the same file `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs`. Settle it: one of the two PRs takes the file.

## Gate (by the rule of #3556: targeted tests, no full heavy lane; a `P2` needs no heavy step)
The body names `pass_start_engagement`, `pass_start_levels`, the motion lib, app `offset_pass_start`, `example_catalog` and clippy on `motion`. Still to run on the final head, and to name in the body with a "Not exercised" section:
- the quick plan (it selects the example suites and `first_part_programs` now);
- app `pocket_pass_start` (2D Pocket Outside changes; on the held implementation the test `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` ran for more than 10 minutes in debug: give its run time here);
- `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `adaptive_pass_start`, `bore_pass_start`, the three catalog suites, clippy on the `camcraft-app` lib.

## Who does the work
The coordinator's worker makes these changes on this branch (it has the fallback and the pins on `issue/3567-ramp-entry-max`). To the session that pushed e7ae538a3: please push no more to this branch, so that the two do not collide again.

Follow-up for the test tool: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3581.

Addressed: the seven review items of the review of e7ae538a3. The commits, pushed as a fast-forward:

- `5d41de71c` fix(2d): ramp only at dead ends the plan marks; named fallback when too short (items 1, 3, 4, 6)
- `0e900246a` test(2d): slope law and ramp pins for the dead-end entry (item 2)
- `1e5fa3bf3` docs(decisions): state the dead-end ramp plainly for #3567 (item 5)
- `d41c2b76a` perf(2d): thin the dead-end ramp's lead within the arc fit budget

Item 7: this PR keeps `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs`. A comment on #3566 tells it to drop its copy.

Blocker: #3588. The verifier cost makes the fig8 Outside pocket test take more than 9 minutes in debug (89.6 s on main). The PR body gives the numbers and the steps still to run. The code is ready for a re-read; the gate waits for #3588.

This commit updates the record for the max-tier re-review.

1. The `Changelog:` row names 2D Offset and 2D Pocket Outside. It gives the measured load: at a dead end, the worst sampled start cuts with about 25 percent of the tool disc in uncut stock (12.6 mm2 of 50.3 mm2 for the 4.780 mm band), so the zig-zag cuts a slot at nearly full tool width at 3 degrees.
2. The decision file and the body do not declare a block by #3588. The slow verification of `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` is a test-speed problem, filed as #3587 (`P5`). The verifier speed is #3588 (fix PR #3595, draft). Neither issue blocks #3577.

Readings on head `d41c2b76a`: `pocket_pass_start` 5 passed of 6. The sixth test stopped at 29 min 23 s. The earlier run tripped the 15-min stall watchdog at 961 s. Every other suite is green. Clippy is clean. The light lane has 2 twins green.

Push: `4d464e006` `docs(2d): record the ramp load and the slow-pin split` (`Refs #3567`).

State for the maintainer: the gate proof of this fix (the late-entry pin at 0.00 mm2, and `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge`) is owed to #3588 and #3595. The single test stalls at 61.5 min even with a 60-min stall cap, so no merge until the pin runs. Findings 1-3 of the max review pass; the text item (Changelog load sentence, record) is fixed at `4d464e006`. The PR stays a draft with `needs-rework`.

Performance blocker on this PR, independent of the correctness work.

With #3595 merged (the fast verifier), the single test `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` has run for more than 17 minutes on the refreshed head `d88494f9a` (this branch's `4d464e006` merged with main `9a7de3781`). The run continues to its cap so the data is complete.

Numbers:
- The whole `pocket_pass_start` suite takes 89.6 s on main.
- It takes 92.99 s on #3595's head.
- This one test takes more than 17 minutes on this branch's head.
- An earlier run on `d41c2b76a` stalled at 61.5 minutes with no output.

The slowdown therefore follows this PR's new entry path, not the verifier.

Result: this PR does not merge as it is. The next step is a fresh look at why the ramp path is slow on this case. A larger stall cap is not the fix.

Trial result of this PR on top of #3595 (merge `5bcb0e4a3`, not pushed; parents: #3595 on main `b5ef7c39e`, and head `4d464e006`; the merge is clean).

- Green: motion `pass_start_engagement` 6; app `offset_pass_start` 4, `first_part_programs` 2, `example_catalog` 37, `golden_cl` 33, `conformance` 7.
- **Not finished:** app `pocket_pass_start`. The run was stopped after about 46 minutes (debug). With `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` skipped, the other 5 tests pass in 46.6 s. On #3595 alone the full binary takes 98 s.

So the fix of #3588 did not remove the cost of this PR's ramp in the verifier. The PR stays a draft with `needs-rework`. Next step: a worker measures where the time goes on this branch with the current main (the tangency law of #3593, or the part of `band_reach` that still grows near a wall), and then corrects the cause or reports the options.

Work resumes on this draft: issue-worker-max #3567 rework. Step 1 measures where the time of `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` goes on the current main, in release. Step 2 fixes the dominant cost.

blocked by #3615 (verifier plane cost); no change in this run. The branch now has a plain merge of main (`7e99878da`, no hand edits). The release measurement is on #3615: law (c) `band_reach` takes 153.5 s of 157.7 s for each generation, in `Rest::surface_before`.
